records.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object can be moving relative to one reference frame but not another.
records.evidence_job: Practice FRQ decomposition/navigation using one shared stimulus, connected labeled parts, and an explicit carry-forward of earlier information.
records.student_action: Use the shared stimulus across connected parts, identify what each part needs, and carry an earlier result or interpretation into a later part.
records.intended_reasoning: Practice FRQ decomposition/navigation using one shared stimulus, connected labeled parts, and an explicit carry-forward of earlier information.
records.shared_stimulus: A student stands inside a bus moving east. A backpack rests on the seat while roadside signs pass the window.
parts: (a) Name two useful reference frames in the situation.
(b) For each frame, state whether the backpack is moving or at rest.
(c) Use your answer from (b) to explain why the two descriptions do not conflict.
(d) Write one complete motion statement that explicitly names its reference frame.
records.student_text:
A student stands inside a bus moving east. A backpack rests on the seat while roadside signs pass the window.
(a) Name two useful reference frames in the situation.
(b) For each frame, state whether the backpack is moving or at rest.
(c) Use your answer from (b) to explain why the two descriptions do not conflict.
(d) Write one complete motion statement that explicitly names its reference frame.
records.student_html:
A student stands inside a bus moving east. A backpack rests on the seat while roadside signs pass the window.

  1. Name two useful reference frames in the situation.
  2. For each frame, state whether the backpack is moving or at rest.
  3. Use your answer from (b) to explain why the two descriptions do not conflict.
  4. Write one complete motion statement that explicitly names its reference frame.
Show your reasoning here.
records.answer: Bus/passenger and Earth/road frames; the backpack is at rest in the bus frame and moving east in the road frame; both are valid relative descriptions.
records.solution_text: Bus/passenger and Earth/road frames; the backpack is at rest in the bus frame and moving east in the road frame; both are valid relative descriptions.
records.solution_html: Bus/passenger and Earth/road frames; the backpack is at rest in the bus frame and moving east in the road frame; both are valid relative descriptions.

part d integrates shared stimulus and earlier work

records.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object can be moving relative to one reference frame but not another.
records.evidence_job: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_action: Use the scenario evidence to make a physics claim and explain why it is consistent with the target.
records.intended_reasoning: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_text: Kai walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Kai walks at 1 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Kai can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.
records.student_html: Kai walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Kai walks at 1 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Kai can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.
records.answer: Relative to the train, Kai moves east at 1 m/s; relative to the ground, Kai moves east at 10 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
records.solution_text: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.
records.solution_html: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.

records.primary_i_can: I can identify the reference frame used in a motion description.
records.evidence_job: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_action: Use the scenario evidence to make a physics claim and explain why it is consistent with the target.
records.intended_reasoning: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_text: A motion description says, “The backpack remains beside Sam on the seat while trees move backward past the window.” Identify the reference frame used when the backpack is described as remaining beside Sam, and cite the cue.
records.student_html: A motion description says, “The backpack remains beside Sam on the seat while trees move backward past the window.” Identify the reference frame used when the backpack is described as remaining beside Sam, and cite the cue.
records.answer: The vehicle/passenger frame; the backpack stays at a fixed position relative to the passenger/seat.
records.solution_text: A reference frame is the object or coordinate system used to judge position and motion. “Beside the passenger on the seat” fixes the backpack relative to the vehicle.
records.solution_html: A reference frame is the object or coordinate system used to judge position and motion. “Beside the passenger on the seat” fixes the backpack relative to the vehicle.

records.primary_i_can: I can compare motion from two different points of view and explain why everyday motion is usually described relative to Earth’s surface.
records.evidence_job: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_action: Use the scenario evidence to make a physics claim and explain why it is consistent with the target.
records.intended_reasoning: Explain, compare, or justify the target idea using the scenario evidence without changing the stated frame, quantity, or representation.
records.student_text: A passenger on a bus says a phone on the seat is at rest. A person on the sidewalk says the phone is moving east with the bus. Compare the two descriptions and explain why using Earth’s surface is convenient for ordinary travel descriptions.
records.student_html: A passenger on a bus says a phone on the seat is at rest. A person on the sidewalk says the phone is moving east with the bus. Compare the two descriptions and explain why using Earth’s surface is convenient for ordinary travel descriptions.
records.answer: Both descriptions can be correct because they use different reference frames. The phone is at rest in the bus frame and moving in the Earth/sidewalk frame. Earth’s surface is a convenient shared everyday frame.
records.solution_text: Motion is relative. Changing the frame changes the measured position/velocity, not the physical object. Earth’s surface is commonly used because it is stable and shared for everyday locations.
records.solution_html: Motion is relative. Changing the frame changes the measured position/velocity, not the physical object. Earth’s surface is commonly used because it is stable and shared for everyday locations.
